convoLines.text: "What did you do for fun? Before. The thing you'd do on a perfect Saturday."
"The free things. Turns out they were the expensive ones."
"Well — I was a baker — fun was whatever I could steal between shifts. Now fun is watching the fire and not being afraid. It's a downgrade and an upgrade."
"Still on what you did for fun."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Daniela always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Austin grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Austin is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"I clean up other people's messes quietly. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Anyway — I should get going."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"When's the last time you really laughed?"
"Stealing joy. I like that. We should steal more of it. Don't look away from this."
"Listen to me — Three days ago. Someone dropped a whole basket of tubers and we just stood there laughing. It wasn't even funny. It was the standing there."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on the last time you laughed. Good talking."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"That can wait — it isn't going anywhere. What's on your mind?"
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Their eyes do the math before their mouth does. You can see the calculation happening.
"I wasn't a midwife. I was an ER nurse. If the wrong people know, it doesn't fall on me. It falls on them."
Aigerim looks at you, level. "I told you the truth. You can keep poking it, but it's told."
"That again?" Aigerim sighs. "I confessed that already. I'm not confessing it twice for dramatic effect."
"You're really going to make me say it again?" Aigerim rubs their face. "Fine — but it's the same truth as last time."
"We went over this," Aigerim says, a little tired. "I already told you the truth about that."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Take care out there."
"Can I tell you something? Before the scattering, I ran when I should have stayed. I think about it every day."
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
You walk to the cache spot with Aaron. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
"Between us — Thank you for hearing it. I needed someone to know — and I needed it to stop with you."
"What are you hoping for? Not the big stuff. The small thing."
"Take your time."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"About that question — What's the most useful thing you've learned since we got here?"
"The fundamental skill. Everything else is decoration. That's my read."
The warmth pulls back a notch. They're weighing something.
"Still on the most useful thing you've learned. Makes sense to me."
"...Never mind me. What were you going to say?"
"Last time things were different. They always are." "Since Daniela died... I keep expecting to see Daniela at the fire. Stupid."
"I clean up other people's messes quietly for Daniela, now. Feels right. Feels like the least I can do."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."

"So." They look at the fire for a moment.

"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
Aigerim: "I've heard good things about The Bloodied. We should link with them — we'd be stronger together."
"All right — let's ask them." You carry the proposal to The Bloodied.
"What do you make of all this? Really."
"Bleak. Probably true. I keep looking for the part where it's not."
"I think we're an experiment someone forgot to label. And the unlabeled part is what scares me — it means nobody's coming to check the results."
"Still on what you make of all this. I mean it."
"Anyway — that's my problem, not yours. What did you want?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "I dreamed Daniela was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Austin nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)

lines: d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Daniela Jain is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d41: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d41: 🕯️ Daniela is dead — and the dead hold no treaties. Every link Haven has shakes.

d41: Emberhold watches to see if Haven holds without its dead. The bond is young — they're still deciding what Haven is, and grief delays the verdict. They'll test the link — count on it, unless Haven answers first: send grain (1,500 kcal), send a speaker (2 days), or let the silence answer. (Trust -8.)
d41: 🕯️ Daniela Jain is dead — the expedition. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d41: What Daniela kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d41: "Daniela's gone." Isaac looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Daniela." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d41: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Leroy blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Wound Care (Level 1). Clean it, close it, cover it. Pressure stops bleeding. Clean water is better than dirty hands.
d41: ⚡ TECHNIQUE UNLOCKED: Precise Mend! Your healing knows where to go. +50% effectiveness. (Your knowledge of Wound Care amplifies your field_medicine.)
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Animal Behavior (Level 1). Most animals flee. Give them an escape route and they take it. Cornered animals fight.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Herbal Medicine (Level 1). Willow bark = aspirin. Yarrow stops bleeding. Plantain draws out infection. The pharmacy is outside.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Camp Cooking (Level 1). Cooking uses half the water, +10% kcal. Once per day: add a Secret Ingredient (a random inventory item) — 50% delicious (+morale), 50% educational.
d41: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Daniela Jain, 41 days. The mantle passes to Leroy Robinson.
d41: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Leroy Robinson, 56 — a Veterinarian. Their hands know different work now: Green Whisper.
d41: The village's quarrel was with Daniela — and Daniela is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d41: At the grave, Isaac, Austin, Aigerim and 5 more speak for Leroy — "Daniela trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d41: The fire knew Leroy before the Codex did — their name already carried weight here.
